- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly to avoid missing downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–2% for the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; apply a lagged correction by reducing forecast 1–3% on the day after sentiment reversal.
- Model tends to overforecast in the short-term (1–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; use a 3-day smoothing filter to dampen noise.
- In periods of high sentiment volatility, model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 10–15% downward bias for the 10–14 day horizon if sentiment is mixed or declining.
- If sentiment is consistently 0.00 over 3+ consecutive days, model underperforms; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to account for potential rebound.
